Subject: Invoice 7891 failed — acquirer AVS mismatch (need next steps)

Hi Mina,

We just received an email from our acquirer that the charge for invoice 7891 (Feb 1, 2027, $12,400) was declined by the acquirer due to an AVS (billing address) mismatch. Stripe's decline message shows: "card_decline — acquirer_declined (AVS mismatch)".

Attached the invoice for reference (invoice_7891.pdf). The customer has confirmed the card is authorized for Redwood, but their bank is requesting stronger proof on file.

Can you:
- Confirm whether Redwood can retry the collection and what evidence you can present to the acquirer?
- Let us know if we should update the billing address on file or provide a signed authorization instead.

This is blocking our reporting — appreciate a quick path forward.

Thanks,
Susan Park
Director, Finance
BrightLeaf Analytics

Attachment: invoice_7891.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice 7891 failed — acquirer AVS mismatch (need next steps)

Hi Susan — thanks for flagging and for the invoice. Sorry for the disruption. We've seen this scenario a few times where the acquirer treats an AVS mismatch as a hard decline even when the cardholder confirms authorization. Two quick paths we can take:

1) Customer self-serve card update: we can send BrightLeaf a secure hosted card-update link (PCI-compliant). Once the new card details are collected, we attempt an immediate retry. This is lowest-friction.

2) Manual retry with evidence: if BrightLeaf prefers we retry on the existing card, we will open a support case with Stripe and submit an evidence packet to the acquirer (invoice, signed authorization, billing address, merchant contact). The acquirer sometimes accepts an evidence packet and reverses the decline; this is not guaranteed.

If you want option (2), please confirm you give Redwood permission to share the signed authorization with Stripe/acquirer and attach the signed form here. If you go with (1), let me know and I will trigger the update link.

I'll loop Marcus (payments ops) to propose the timing for a manual retry and what exact artifacts we need.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hey team — I reviewed the Stripe event and the acquirer decline. Quick summary and recommended ops: 

Summary:
- Stripe decline: acquirer_declined (AVS mismatch).
- No evidence of a chargeback yet — only an authorization/charge failure.

Recommended next steps (we can execute within 48 hrs):
1) If BrightLeaf updates card (preferred) — we will immediately attempt a normal capture on the new payment method.

2) If they want us to retry on the same card:
   - We need a signed authorization form from BrightLeaf (PDF) that explicitly authorizes Redwood to charge the card and includes the billing address on file.
   - We will open a Stripe support ticket and submit the evidence packet to the acquirer (invoice_7891.pdf, signed authorization, copy of the merchant's billing statement, contact).
   - ETA: schedule manual retry 2027-02-28T11:00:00-08:00 (contains a short window for the acquirer's review).

Notes: sometimes the acquirer rejects evidence if AVS mismatch is systemic (issuer policy) — in that case we recommend the customer update card or provide an alternate payment method. Also if this is an EU-issued card there are additional AVS/3DS rules to consider; looks like BrightLeaf's BIN is US-based so standard AVS should apply.

I attach a short checklist I use for evidence submissions. If we get the signed PDF from BrightLeaf and their explicit permission to share it with Stripe, I'll open the support case and set the retry window.

--
Marcus Lin
Payments Operations, Redwood Inference
